hi, my tomato plants are acting weird. the leaves at the bottom are turning yellow but the ones at the top look okay. what do you think is going on and how can i fix the soil?

The yellow‑bottom‑leaf syndrome is usually a clue that something is off in the root zone, not that the plant is “sick” in the upper canopy. A few common culprits and a quick “how‑to‑fix‑the‑soil” recipe are listed below, all of which you can address without major upheaval.

---

## 1. What the yellow bottom leaves are **telling you**  

| Symptom | Likely cause (soil‑related) | Why the bottom leaves go yellow first |
|---------|----------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Yellowing, then browning of the oldest leaves | **Nitrogen deficiency** or **pH imbalance** | Older leaves are the first to be sacrificed when the plant can’t pull enough nitrogen from the soil. |
| Yellow‑green, limp leaves, especially at the base | **Water‑logging / poor drainage** | Roots sitting in soggy soil can’t take up nutrients, so the plant starves the oldest foliage. |

The “gnawed‑looking” lesions on tomato stems are almost always a sign of a **pest** or a **secondary infection** that follows a wound. Below is a quick diagnostic checklist, plus a targeted treatment plan that you can start today.

## 2. Identifying the culprit behind the stem “bite marks”

|---------|-------------------|-------------------|
